claims.content: To allow the Operator to enter, edit, and export information about a system problem via a separate display.

goal.raw_text: To allow the Operator to enter, edit, and export information about a system problem via a separate display.

claims.content: Operator
The Operator must be authenticated and assigned a security level, as user security levels are assigned at the command level, device, mode, workstation, and system function.
The system shall provide a separate display that allows the user to enter information about a system problem.
The Problem Work Order data shall be editable and exportable to ASCII delimited files by the user.
The Operator initiates the use case by accessing the separate display that allows entry of information about a system problem.

trigger.raw_text: The Operator initiates the use case by accessing the separate display that allows entry of information about a system problem.

claims.content: The Operator accesses the separate display that allows entry of information about a system problem.
The Operator enters or edits information about a system problem in the Problem Work Order interface.
The system validates and stores the entered Problem Work Order data, including fields such as Problem Work Order ID, Date, Time, Operator, Problem Work Order Status ID, and Description.
The system associates the entered Problem Work Order with relevant Personnel via the Problem Work Order Personnel entity, linking Personnel ID to the work order.
The system updates the Problem Work Order Status based on operator input or system rules, reflecting current state (e.g., open, closed).
The Operator may export the Problem Work Order data to ASCII delimited files for reporting or external use.
If the Operator attempts to update log entries other than for their own login, for the current day and current shift, the system shall not allow the update.

The Problem Work Order Log will be generated automatically with failure information at the time of failure, and some input fields in this log will allow the operator to input status and emergency notification information.
If the Operator attempts to modify log entries for a time period other than their own login, current day, and current shift, the system shall not allow the update.

If the Operator lacks sufficient security level privileges to access or modify Problem Work Order data at the command, device, mode, workstation, or system function level, the system shall deny the operation.
The Problem Work Order Log is generated automatically with failure information at the time of failure, and includes operator-input status and emergency notification information.
The Problem Work Order data is stored and associated with assigned Personnel via the Problem Work Order Personnel entity.
The Problem Work Order Status is updated to reflect the current state (e.g., open, closed) based on operator input or system rules.
The Operator’s actions are recorded in logs that include timestamp, operator ID, and unit where the command was issued, and these logs are not editable by users.
